A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MCDIFFUSE work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–I are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original six-benchmark evaluations, hyperparameter experiments, generation-length analyses, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds harness-based evaluations, compute-matched baseline comparisons, and FLOP measurements.

M1.justification: The confidence reward, PUCT selection, stochastic rollouts, value mixing, backpropagation, and final visit-count selection remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–5. The added confidence-bias discussion explains existing components rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, MATH500, ARC Challenge, GPQA-Diamond, MBPP, and HumanEval. The added harness evaluations and compute comparisons retain these datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: V2 Appendix D.5 and Table 9 add confidence-reranked best-of-N sampling and beam search over slot-order decisions across all six benchmarks. These introduce substantive inference-compute controls absent from v1; the original model and sequential/random-order comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Appendices D.4–D.5 add LM-Eval-Harness evaluations using task-specific prompting, answer extraction, and parsing, alongside stated matched decoding/configurations and compute-matched controls. These supplement the retained generic chain-of-thought evaluations. Table 3 also introduces total FLOPs as a cost metric.

E4.justification: The added analyses test whether gains persist under the evaluation harness and whether additional inference compute alone explains them, using the new controls in Appendix D.5. Cross-benchmark FLOP accounting supplements the existing runtime analysis. Earlier sensitivity, sequentiality, token-length, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: The three-run statement, seeds 21/42/84, Table 1 uncertainties, and existing significance/effect-size analyses are unchanged. The new tables provide point estimates without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure or explicitly changing run counts.

E6.justification: V2 Tables 8–9 add harness results: the proposed method, labelled DiffuSearch there, averages 74.53%, versus ReFusion's 67.98%, best-of-N's 61.82%, and beam search's 63.84%. Table 3 adds FLOP results. Table 1 remains identical, including MCDIFFUSE's 68.52% average; the harness scores are additional results under different conditions, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, reward and value definitions, search equations, and appendix rollout derivations retain their mathematical substance. Changes simplify notation and adjust an illustrative Q-value; no formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free MCTS slot planning, benchmark competitiveness, strategic non-sequential generation, and exploration breadth. The added evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds discussion of confidence favouring short, easy continuations and how existing search components mitigate that risk. It interprets the new controls as evidence against a compute-only explanation and adds qualifications about the speed–accuracy frontier and evaluation being confined to ReFusion.

D1.justification: Appendices D.4–D.5 newly identify the evaluation harness, task-specific answer handling, confidence-based reranking, and beam search over slot decisions. Existing hardware and implementation settings remain unchanged. Best-of-N counts, beam widths, and the precise compute-matching procedure are not supplied.

R1.justification: Section 7 replaces the visual-diffusion origin discussion with Austin et al.'s discrete diffusion work and references to Shi, Sahoo, and Ou. V2 also adds Damani and Biderman citations and replaces the LLaDA2.0 citation with LLaDA2.0-Uni. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized wording, heading, and notation edits, expands several explanatory paragraphs, and adds Appendices D.4–D.5 and acknowledgements. The overall narrative structure remains intact. The unexplained DiffuSearch name in the new appendix introduces a terminology inconsistency.

P2.justification: V2 adds the FLOP table and two harness-comparison tables; Table 9 repeats Table 8's ReFusion/proposed-method rows while adding controls. Figure 1 is resized and its caption/action label and illustrative value are corrected. Other figures retain their content, with localized resizing, repositioning, and table-spacing changes.

improvement.justification: V2 partially addresses v1's lack of compute-matched controls and harness-based validation, while FLOP reporting and explicit applicability limits improve transparency. The benefit is limited by unspecified matching budgets and baseline parameters, absent uncertainty in the new comparisons, and the unexplained DiffuSearch label. These additions strengthen the evidence without fully resolving its reproducibility limitations.
